scenes.why: The hook is the guide's own title: the question it answers, as a person would put it.

copy.text: Identify which heating, cooling, ventilation, and outdoor-water systems the property actually has.
Check manuals and existing service records before choosing work.
Arrange heating service or inspection appropriate to the equipment.
Test smoke and carbon monoxide alarms according to their instructions.

scenes.why: The guide's own checklist, the first sentence of each item, ticked in as it is read.

scenes.why: The turn: the product the guide itself hands over to, named and shown on its real screen, captioned with its listing's line closest to what the guide teaches. Screen: "A couple of things need a look" (Your home now: what's wrong, what to care for, what's coming up and what's handled, with the fridge and a dripping tap flagged.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "A sentence about your home's condition, and the few things worth doing Fall home"; focus on "Wrong, To care for, Coming up, Handled".
Ends on where to read the whole guide, with the product beneath it: the viewer leaves with the next step, not only a pitch.

reasoning.decision: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "tag"
reasoning.because: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "tag": things in the home are tagged, so scenes rise like a tag being lifted.
Camera "dolly": constant forward movement for a high-energy feed.
Grounds ink → light → light → accent: a cool accent, so a darker ground is used for contrast at a turn.
Sound-on placement: every transition, landing and reveal has a cue, and the bed ducks under the brand moment.
Each scene is held for the time its words take to read on YouTube Short (0.26s a word), inside 18–45s.
